sections.h2: Where does an Ohio County, Kentucky owner pay the tax bill?
sections.html:
Payment goes to the sheriff's tax office at 301 South Main Street in Hartford. Mail goes to PO Box 186, Hartford, KY 42347, and the office line is 270-298-4444.

The county's sheriff page lists weekday counter hours of 8 a.m.-4 p.m. and a half day (8 a.m.-noon) on each month's first and last Saturday. A drop box is mounted on the door for after-hours payments. Postmarks are honored on mailed checks, and cash should never go in an envelope. Card payments can be made at the counter or through a link on the sheriff's website.

The sheriff does not set values. Questions about an assessment, a mailing address or an exemption go to the county's Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) at 270-298-4433.

sections.h2: How large is Ohio County, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Ohio County is big and sparsely settled. It spans 587 square miles of land, the fifth-largest of Kentucky's 120 counties, with about 40 residents per square mile in 2020. Hartford is the seat of government and Beaver Dam is the largest city. Centertown, Fordsville, McHenry and Rockport are the other cities, and Rosine is a census-designated place. The Rough River crosses the county, and the Green River marks its southwestern edge.

The legislature carved the county out of Hardin County in 1798, and its coal mines made it well known across the region. In January 1865 Confederate cavalry burned the Hartford courthouse, although the county records had been carried out beforehand.

The head count tells its own story. Ohio County had 1,223 people in 1800, peaked at 27,642 in 1910 and fell to 17,725 by 1960 as farms and mines shed workers. It climbed back to 21,765 in 1980 and has hovered near 24,000 since 2010. Census Bureau figures sketch the housing picture today.

  • The July 2025 estimate counts 23,934 residents, 0.7 percent above the April 2020 base.
  • A typical owned house is worth $121,400 in the 2020 to 2024 survey, and owners with a mortgage report $1,105 in monthly costs.
  • Homeowners hold 77.2 percent of the 9,107 households.
  • Median household income is $57,798, and 15.3 percent of residents live below the poverty line.
  • Residents aged 65 or older make up 20.6 percent of the population.
  • The county has 10,377 housing units, and builders pulled only 3 permits in 2025.

sections.h2: What are the Ohio County payment periods and penalties?
sections.html:
Bills become payable on October 1. The sheriff publishes the calendar below, and the assessment date behind every bill is January 1.

Ohio County collection calendar (Ohio County Sheriff's Office, property tax information page)
DatesAmount due
October 1 to November 1Bill less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to 31Face amount plus 5 percent
February 1 to April 15Face amount plus 21 percent
After April 15Bill transfers to the County Clerk

The state schedule in KRS 134.015 shows 10 percent for the same stretch, so get an exact payoff from the tax office for your own parcel.

No bill by October 10? The sheriff wants a call, and a duplicate goes out by mail, fax or email. A copy sent elsewhere is a one-time courtesy. The PVA alone changes the standing mailing address.

sections.h2: What happens to Ohio County bills left unpaid on April 15?
sections.html:
Prior-year payments stop at the sheriff on April 15 and move to the Ohio County Clerk, at 301 S Main St, Suite 201 in Hartford (weekdays 8 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; recording desk 270-298-4423). The clerk's delinquent tax page announced a tax sale for October 23, 2025, which has passed, so ask for the next date.

  • The bill turns into a recorded lien, and the Department of Revenue says interest starts at 1 percent a month.
  • Bidders over three certificates in the county, five statewide or $10,000 in total must register with the state.
  • For a listed house, get a written payoff from the clerk because it rises monthly.

sections.h2: Where does an Ohio County owner turn to contest a value?
sections.html: Begin with the PVA at 270-298-4433, where a conference must happen while the spring inspection period is open. Bring comparable sales, repair estimates and photos. A failed conference leads to a form at the County Clerk, then a local three-person board, then the state Board of Tax Appeals. The PVA appeal guide spells out each deadline, including 30 days to reach the state board.

sections.h2: Which breaks reduce an Ohio County tax bill?
sections.html:
Owners aged 65 or older, or totally disabled, who live in the house may claim the homestead exemption. The sheriff's page adds that a 70 percent VA rating or a 100 percent Social Security disability finding can qualify, and the PVA decides each case. The deduction is a set dollar figure that the state resets every two years, and a buyer must apply again.

Farmland gets its own treatment. Acreage in farm use is taxed at agricultural value rather than market value, which can matter a great deal where 76 percent of residents live in rural areas.

sections.h2: What does an Ohio County seller owe beyond the tax bill?
sections.html:
The seller carries the state transfer tax: 50 cents per $500 of declared value, rounded up (KRS 142.050). At the $121,400 county median that is 243 units and $121.50, due before the clerk accepts the deed.

  • Confirm with the sheriff who is paying this year's bill.
  • Ask the clerk about any recorded lien or certificate.
  • Put a tax-bill mailing address in the deed, as KRS 382.135 demands.

sections.h2: What do owners and renters pay in Ohio County?
sections.html:
Monthly housing costs are low by national standards. Owners without a mortgage report a median of $395 a month, and those with a mortgage report $1,105. Median gross rent is $739, and the average household has 2.58 people. Per capita income is $28,772.

The Census counts 10,377 housing units against 9,107 occupied households, so roughly 1,270 units sit empty, are used seasonally or are held for sale. A seller whose house has been vacant should expect a buyer's inspector to look hard at the roof, plumbing and utilities, and should ask the sheriff whether a vacant property has any special tax status. Nonemployer businesses numbered 1,351 in 2024, a sign that self-employed owners and small landlords hold a meaningful share of local property.

sections.h2: Which parts of Ohio County's economy affect home sales?
sections.html:
Retail, health care and transportation carry the local economy. Census data show $255.6 million in retail sales for 2022, which works out to $10,876 for every resident, along with $111.7 million in health care and social assistance receipts and $58.4 million in transportation and warehousing. Accommodation and food services brought in $23.3 million.

The county counted 371 employer establishments and 7,858 jobs in 2023, a 14.3 percent jump in employment over 2022, and its annual payroll reached $265.2 million. Workers travel 28.1 minutes each way on average, and 85.1 percent of households have a broadband subscription.

The people side matters to a buyer too. About 91.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is low. Just 13.9 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, 8.8 percent of people under 65 lack health insurance, and 874 residents are veterans. Few homes change hands in any single small town, which makes pricing a house in Fordsville, Rockport or McHenry harder than in Beaver Dam.

faqs.q: Which Ohio County office takes tax payments?
faqs.a: The sheriff's tax office in Hartford, at 301 South Main Street. A mailed check goes to PO Box 186, Hartford, KY 42347.

faqs.q: When does a penalty begin on an Ohio County property tax bill?
faqs.a: On January 1, when a 5 percent penalty applies through January 31. Paying between November 2 and December 31 costs the face amount only.

faqs.q: Can a house with an unpaid tax bill still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Payoff comes out of the proceeds, using a figure from the sheriff before April 15 or from the County Clerk after it.

faqs.q: Whom do I call to question my Ohio County valuation?
faqs.a: The PVA, 270-298-4433. Values are outside the sheriff's authority.

faqs.q: What transfer tax would a seller pay at the Ohio County median price?
faqs.a: $121.50 on a $121,400 sale, which counts as 243 units of $500.
